info.title: Apache Iggy HTTP API
info.description: REST API of the Apache Iggy server. Most routes need a bearer credential: either an access token from a login or refresh route, or a raw personal access token. Names and numeric IDs are both accepted wherever a path takes a stream, topic, consumer group, user or consumer. In a cluster, a follower forwards control plane writes to the primary. The web UI routes under `/ui` are not described here.

post.summary: Log in with a username and password
post.description: Unauthenticated. Wrong credentials and an inactive user are answered with 400. With external authentication enabled, an unknown username is checked with the external service: a refusal is 400, and a failed check is 503. Also answers 503 if the node has not finished replaying its log after a restart.

200.description: An access token for the user.

post.description: Unauthenticated. The current access token is sent in the body. The presented token is not revoked and stays valid until it expires. Tokens from trusted external issuers cannot be refreshed.

200.description: A new access token for the same user.

delete.description: Ends the server-side session for the presented credential. The bearer token itself is not revoked and stays valid until it expires.

200.description: Every user.
The created user.

get.description: Reading your own user (by `me`, your ID or your username) needs no permission. Reading another user requires `read_users` or `manage_users`.

200.description: The user and its permissions.

put.description: Changes the username, the status, or both. Requires the `manage_users` permission.
Changing your own password needs no permission; changing another user's needs `manage_users`. A wrong current password is answered with 400, and an unknown user with 404.

post.summary: Log in with a personal access token
post.description: Unauthenticated. An unknown or expired token is answered with 401, and a token whose user is inactive with 400.

200.description: An access token for the token's owner.

get.description: Requires the `poll_messages` permission for the topic.

parameters.name: consumer_id
parameters.description: Consumer ID or name. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: consumer_kind
parameters.description: Defaults to `consumer`. `consumer_group` is refused with 400.

parameters.name: partition_id
parameters.description: Partition ID. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Where to start polling. Defaults to `offset`. The single letters `o`, `t`, `f`, `l` and `n` are also accepted.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Offset, or timestamp in microseconds, for the `offset` and `timestamp` kinds. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: JSON-encoded `PartitionContext` from an earlier reply, such as `{"incarnation":1,"owner_generation":2,"metadata_op":3}`. The poll is refused with 400 if the partition was recreated or changed owner since, and with 503 if this node has not yet seen that context.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: auto_commit
parameters.description: Must be false here. A poll that stores its offset is a write, so `true` is refused with 400: send it as `POST .../messages/deferred` instead.

200.description: The polled messages.

post.description: Requires the `send_messages` permission for the topic.

parameters.name: ack
parameters.description: `replicated` waits for the quorum commit and answers 201. `none` answers 202 as soon as the batch is dispatched.

201.description: The batch was committed. The body lists where it landed.

202.description: The batch was accepted for dispatch. Commit was not awaited. The response has no body.

get.summary: Poll messages, waiting for them to arrive
get.description: Requires the `poll_messages` permission for the topic. Waits until `min_count` messages are available or `wait_us` passes, then answers like `GET .../messages`. The wait limits are checked before authentication. Answers 503 with Retry-After when the server has too many deferred polls waiting.

parameters.name: consumer_id
parameters.description: Consumer ID or name. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: consumer_kind
parameters.description: Defaults to `consumer`. `consumer_group` is refused with 400.

parameters.name: partition_id
parameters.description: Partition ID. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Where to start polling. Defaults to `offset`. The single letters `o`, `t`, `f`, `l` and `n` are also accepted.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Offset, or timestamp in microseconds, for the `offset` and `timestamp` kinds. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: JSON-encoded `PartitionContext` from an earlier reply, such as `{"incarnation":1,"owner_generation":2,"metadata_op":3}`. The poll is refused with 400 if the partition was recreated or changed owner since, and with 503 if this node has not yet seen that context.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: wait_us
parameters.description: How long to wait for `min_count` messages, in microseconds. At most 600000000. 0 answers at once.

parameters.name: min_count
parameters.description: Answer as soon as this many messages are available. At least 1 and no more than `count`.

parameters.name: max_bytes
parameters.description: Upper bound on the reply size in bytes. At least 344.

parameters.name: request_timeout_us
parameters.description: Server-side budget for the whole request, in microseconds, from 1 to 630000000. When `wait_us` is above 0 it must be at least `wait_us` plus 1000000.

parameters.name: auto_commit
parameters.description: Must be false here. `true` is refused with 400: use `POST` on this path.

200.description: The polled messages.

post.summary: Poll messages and store the offset, waiting for them to arrive
post.description: Requires the `poll_messages` permission for the topic. Waits until `min_count` messages are available or `wait_us` passes, then answers like `GET .../messages`. The wait limits are checked before authentication. Answers 503 with Retry-After when the server has too many deferred polls waiting. With `auto_commit=true` the poll stores the consumer offset and counts as a write. No body is read.

parameters.name: consumer_id
parameters.description: Consumer ID or name. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: consumer_kind
parameters.description: Defaults to `consumer`. `consumer_group` is refused with 400.

parameters.name: partition_id
parameters.description: Partition ID. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Where to start polling. Defaults to `offset`. The single letters `o`, `t`, `f`, `l` and `n` are also accepted.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Offset, or timestamp in microseconds, for the `offset` and `timestamp` kinds. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: JSON-encoded `PartitionContext` from an earlier reply, such as `{"incarnation":1,"owner_generation":2,"metadata_op":3}`. The poll is refused with 400 if the partition was recreated or changed owner since, and with 503 if this node has not yet seen that context.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: wait_us
parameters.description: How long to wait for `min_count` messages, in microseconds. At most 600000000. 0 answers at once.

parameters.name: min_count
parameters.description: Answer as soon as this many messages are available. At least 1 and no more than `count`.

parameters.name: max_bytes
parameters.description: Upper bound on the reply size in bytes. At least 344.

parameters.name: request_timeout_us
parameters.description: Server-side budget for the whole request, in microseconds, from 1 to 630000000. When `wait_us` is above 0 it must be at least `wait_us` plus 1000000.

parameters.name: auto_commit
parameters.description: Store the consumer offset after polling. The offset may advance before the response arrives, and a successful response does not confirm the commit.

200.description: The polled messages.

get.description: Requires the `manage_servers` permission, whatever groups are asked for. Pages through the log of metadata changes, or through the current state of the selected groups when `from=current`, so a client can follow changes without listing resources again. Exactly one of `from` and `after` is required. Unknown, repeated or malformed query keys are refused with 400, including `consistency`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Where to start: the oldest retained change, the newest, or a page of the current state.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor from `next` of an earlier reply.

parameters.name: current_after
parameters.description: Token from `current_page_token`. Only with `from=current`.

parameters.name: groups
parameters.description: Comma-separated groups to include. Absent or empty means all.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only changes at or after this time, in microseconds. Not with `latest` or `current`.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Only changes at or before this time, in microseconds. Not with `latest` or `current`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size.

200.description: A page of changes or current items.

bearerAuth.description: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, with `Bearer` written exactly so. The token is an access token from `POST /users/login`, `POST /personal-access-tokens/login` or `POST /users/refresh-token`, or a raw personal access token. The server tries it as a JWT first and then as a personal access token. An access token stops working once its user is deleted, even if the ID is reused. Tokens from configured trusted external issuers are also accepted, and act as the user the issuer names, who must exist, be active and not be root.

UserIdOrMe.name: user_id
UserIdOrMe.description: User ID or username, or `me` for the caller. A user named `me` can still be read by ID.

ConsumerId.name: consumer_id
ConsumerId.description: Consumer ID or name. HTTP always uses a regular consumer, never a consumer group.

PatName.name: name
PatName.description: Name of the personal access token.

Consistency.name: consistency
Consistency.description: `serializable` reads from this node's local state, which may lag the primary. `linearizable` reads at the primary: a follower that forwards requests relays the read to the primary, or for message and offset reads waits for the primary's commit point. A follower that does not forward redirects with 307 when it can resolve the primary's address, and answers 503 otherwise. Unknown values are rejected with 400.

IggyView.description: Current consensus view number. Set on success and redirect responses when the node runs consensus. Never set on errors or on `/ping`.

IggyAppliedOp.description: Metadata operation number the serving node has applied. Set on success and redirect responses. Never set on errors or on `/ping`.

IggyDurabilityCommitted.description: Durability the commit achieved under the topic's message policy.

IggyDurabilityNone.description: Always `none`: the batch was dispatched but its commit was not awaited.

Location.description: URL of the same request on the primary.

ContentDisposition.description: Marks the response as a file download.

TemporaryRedirect.description: Only for `consistency=linearizable` on a follower that does not forward requests. Repeat the request against the primary at `Location`.

BadRequest.description: The request was rejected: an invalid identifier, a failed validation, or a business error such as a duplicate name. A path or query string that cannot be parsed, or malformed JSON, is answered with a plain text body instead. A typed user header the server cannot decode is answered with 400 JSON.

Unauthenticated.description: The bearer credential is missing, invalid or expired.

Forbidden.description: The caller lacks the permission this route needs.

SessionConflict.description: The server session ID minted for this credential is owned by another user. Retrying will not help.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The body is larger than `http.max_request_size`. The body is JSON with code `payload_too_large` on message and offset routes and when the node was forwarding the request, and plain text otherwise. The connection is closed on HTTP/1.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request has no `Content-Type: application/json` header.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The JSON body does not match the expected shape.

TooManyRequests.description: Too many requests in flight: this session's writes, or the relayed requests the target node accepts for this credential. Wait for them to finish, then retry.

BadGateway.description: The node forwarded the request to the primary and the forward failed after sending, or the primary's reply was too large to relay. The outcome is unknown.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A temporary condition, such as no caught-up primary, a node still recovering, or a busy node. Safe to retry after `Retry-After`.

GatewayTimeout.description: No reply arrived in time. For writes the outcome is unknown and the write may still commit.

Identifier.description: A numeric ID or a name, 1 to 255 bytes long. A value that parses as an unsigned 32-bit integer is used as a numeric ID. Anything else is used as a name, so a resource whose name is all digits can only be addressed by its ID.

ErrorResponse.description: Error body returned by every route.

id.description: Iggy error code, or the HTTP status code for errors raised by the HTTP layer itself.

code.description: Error name in snake case, for example `stream_id_not_found` or `not_found`.

field.description: Request field the error relates to, when known.

ByteSize.description: Byte size as a string with a unit, for example `0 B`, `1 KiB` or `1.234 KB`.

Expiry.description: Expiry in microseconds. 0 means the server default and 18446744073709551615 (the largest unsigned 64-bit value) means never expire.

value.description: Value as text: base64 for `raw`, `0x` and the hexadecimal IEEE 754 bits for floats, otherwise the same form a create request takes.

explicit.description: True when the value was set by a client rather than defaulted.

default_value.description: Default value as raw bytes in the encoding of `kind`. Empty when the key has no default.

updatable.description: Can be changed by an update request.

resettable.description: Can be named in the `reset` array of an update request.

read_only.description: Computed by the server; a request cannot set it.

critical.description: A build that cannot read this option refuses the resource instead of ignoring it.

access_token.description: Always set by the login and refresh routes.

token.description: Access token (JWT) to send as a bearer token.

expiry.description: Expiry time in seconds since the Unix epoch.

version.description: Client version. Accepted but not used by the HTTP login.

context.description: Client context. Accepted but not used by the HTTP login.

token.description: A current, unexpired access token issued by this server.
Raw token. Store it securely: it cannot be retrieved again.

expiry_at.description: Expiry time, or null if the token never expires.

GlobalPermissions.description: Permissions that apply to every stream.

StreamPermissions.description: Permissions for one stream and its topics.

topics.description: Per-topic permissions keyed by numeric topic ID. Omit or send null for none.

streams.description: Per-stream permissions keyed by numeric stream ID. Omit or send null for none.

options.description: Resource options keyed by option name.
Resource options keyed by option name.

permissions.description: Permissions. Omit or send null for none.

options.description: Options keyed by name. `GET /options/user` lists the keys, their kinds and which can be set at create. Unknown and repeated keys are rejected.

UpdateUser.description: User options to change, as one flat object. Send only the keys to change. `null` keeps the current value. A body that changes nothing is refused with 400.

permissions.description: New permissions. Omit or send null to remove all permissions.

options.description: Resource options keyed by option name.
Resource options keyed by option name.

name.description: Unique stream name, up to 255 bytes.

options.description: Options keyed by name. `GET /options/stream` lists the keys, their kinds and which can be set at create. Unknown and repeated keys are rejected. A stored option sent at the top level instead of inside `options` is refused with 400.

UpdateStream.description: Stream options to change, as one flat object. Send only the keys to change. `null` keeps the current value. A body that changes nothing is refused with 400.

name.description: New stream name, up to 255 bytes.

options.description: Resource options keyed by name, including `compression_algorithm`, `message_expiry` and `max_topic_size`.
Resource options keyed by name, including `compression_algorithm`, `message_expiry` and `max_topic_size`.

members.description: Replica IDs of the nodes that hold the partition.

in_sync_members.description: Replica IDs of the members that are in sync.

options.description: Options keyed by name. `GET /options/topic` lists the keys, their kinds and which can be set at create. Unknown and repeated keys are rejected. A stored option such as `message_expiry` sent at the top level instead of inside `options` is refused with 400.

UpdateTopic.description: Topic options to change, as one flat object. Only `name`, `message_expiry` and `max_topic_size` can be changed; the other topic options are fixed at create. Send only the keys to change. `null` keeps the current value. A body that changes nothing is refused with 400.

name.description: New topic name, up to 255 bytes.

reset.description: Options to return to their defaults.

partitions_count.description: Number of partitions to add, from 1 to 1000.

ConsumerId.description: Consumer ID as a number, or an ID or name as a string. Defaults to 1.

context.description: Fences the store: it is refused if the partition changed since this context was read.

open_files_count.description: File descriptors the server process holds open, 0 when unknown. Can be up to 10 seconds old.

open_files_limit.description: Soft limit on open file descriptors, 0 when unknown.

snapshot_types.description: What to include in the archive.

replica_id.description: The node's VSR replica ID. Key nodes by it, not by position.

ip.description: Address for the caller to connect to.

kind.description: `balanced` picks a partition by round robin. `partition_id` uses the partition in `value`. `messages_key` hashes `value` to pick a partition.

value.description: Base64 bytes, at most 255 before encoding. For `partition_id`, the partition ID as 4 little-endian bytes. For `messages_key`, the key. May be empty only for `balanced`.

HeaderField.description: A typed header key or value.

value.description: Base64 of the value bytes. Numbers are little-endian.

oneOf.description: Raw header bytes that could not be decoded as entries, such as client-side encrypted headers.
Decimal 128-bit ID, or 32 hex digits with optional dashes (UUID form).
Raw header bytes, for example client-side encrypted headers.

SendMessages.description: Only `partitioning`, `messages` and `context` are accepted. Other fields are rejected.

context.description: Fences the send: it is refused if the partition changed since this context was read.

confirmations.description: One entry per partition the batch landed in. Empty when the commit reported no offsets.

base_offset.description: Offset of the first message of the batch in the partition.

partition_id.description: Partition the messages came from. An empty batch may carry a sentinel value instead.

user_headers.description: User headers. An empty array when the message has none.

id.description: Message ID, an unsigned 128-bit integer written as a JSON number.

HeaderKind.description: Value type an option is stored as.

oneOf.description: The same form a config file uses, such as `7 days` or `1 GiB`. A 64-bit value above 2^53 - 1 is sent as a decimal string.

OptionInput.description: One option value: a boolean, a non-negative integer, or a string.

PartitionContext.description: Partition history a request is fenced with. Send back the context from an earlier reply so the server refuses the request if the partition was recreated or changed owner since.

ConsumerKind.description: `consumer` is a single consumer. `external_group` is a group whose membership is managed outside Iggy, so only its offsets are stored here.

log_id.description: Identity of the change log, as 32 hexadecimal digits.

next.description: Cursor to pass as `after` for the next page.

current_page_token.description: Token to pass as `current_after` for the next page of the current phase.

MetadataChangeRecord.description: One change. The fields of the change itself sit alongside these, and depend on `kind`. A kind this server cannot render carries its raw body as base64 in `body`.

actor_user_id.description: Left out when no user made the change.

MetadataCurrentItem.description: One resource in the current phase. Its fields sit alongside `group`.
